decision: The buy box answers the four questions in order: will it fit, when will it arrive, where can I get it today, what does it cost per month
why: Returns come mostly from fit and missed delivery expectations; putting those answers before Add to bag reduces both.
alternative: Description-first layout with specs below the fold.
value: Fewer size exchanges and support contacts (target [value]).

decision: The fit hint comes from review fit votes and the shopper's own kept sizes, and it rewrites itself when you pick a size
why: 'Runs large' alone makes people guess; relating it to the size they usually keep turns it into a recommendation.
value: The size choice carries its own evidence (share of reviewers who sized down).

decision: The delivery cutoff counts down on the shared world clock and is set by store pick capacity, not stock
why: Counter decides whether an order can make the 18:30 carrier pickup; the promise on the page must be the one operations can keep.
value: The same clock drives the PDP countdown and Counter's cutoff plan, so the promise and the operation never disagree.

decision: Unavailable sizes stay in place with a dashed outline and strike, and are announced as sold out
why: Removing them shifts the layout and hides that the size exists; color alone fails for color-blind shoppers.
alternative: Hide sold-out sizes, or gray them with opacity.
value: Readable at AA with no color dependency, and the grid never jumps.

decision: Thumbnails are ARIA tabs and zoom is a CSS transform around the pointer, with a Zoom button for keyboard and touch
why: Fabric texture sells linen; a transform needs no second high-resolution image and no layout work.
alternative: A lightbox with a separate zoom image.
value: Zoom costs zero bytes and works with a mouse, keyboard or touch.

decision: The AI review summary quotes only themes mentioned by 8+ verified buyers, shows theme counts as sources and is checked daily by a person
why: Summaries that invent consensus destroy trust in all reviews; counts let shoppers judge the claim.
value: The summary is auditable from the page: every claim maps to a counted theme.

decision: Frequently bought together comes from 90-day co-purchase pairs, and unticking an item updates the total and the button in place
why: Bundles are the highest-converting cross-sell, but only when the shopper controls what goes in.
alternative: A carousel of 'You may also like'.
value: Higher basket size (target [value]) without surprise items.

decision: A strip of shoppable creator reels that feature this product, each opening the reel with its tagged items
why: Seeing the piece move on a person answers drape and fit questions that photos can't, a pattern popularized by short-video apps.
value: Creator content links straight to purchase, and Circle attributes the sale.
